posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
byc:

a villain that punishes the heroes for having a large hand size

I would be just as happy if this never occurs.  At least.

  • a super-intelligent ape villain

This probably already exists in the form of Treacherous Ape (his card represents an imaginary projection of him, but Tachyon recognizes him as if they've met before, so presumably there was a real one in her past which Dreamy's mind copied for one of her nightmare-creatures).  We can't be sure how closely he resembles Gorilla Grodd, but for legal and originality reasons that's probably for the best.

  • a super scientist hero (like Mr Fantastic, Tachyon isn't on his level I don't believe)

Well, and, I believe you're dead wrong on that.  Also there's Writhe, who is a very direct Mr. Fantastic analogue.

  • an super adaptoid type villain where the villain has all the abilities of a team/group of heroes
  • a parasite/draining type villain that steals the powers of a hero

Either of these would be mechanically nightmarish to accomplish, given how loosely this game defines "powers"…Tachyon has the "power" of super speed, represented by playing lots of cards, but has no Power: effects in her deck representing this (and one which very definitely does not), with the very arguable exception of her base power (the name suggests speed, but hardly exemplifies it).  Given that many characters have no "powers" at all, but just lots of technology (Bunker, Expatriette, Chrono-Ranger, and to a limited extent Unity and Absolute Zero), and that several characters's powers are somewhat loosely defined (Legacy has the superhuman powers of flight and indestructibility, but also a degree of charisma and leadership skill which is only arguably paranormal, some of it probably being derived simply from his personality), I don't think this could be accomplished in game terms to any real degree of effect.  They might make a character who has this as their backstory, but the result would just play like any self-contained villain, having been designed to resemble all the heroes to some limited extent, much as Iron Legacy is designed to resemble his original.

posts.cooked:
I'm not a playtester and I have no real foreknowledge of what may come in Wrath of the Cosmos, but here are my totally premature bold predictions:

Heroes:

We'll get Sky-Scraper and Captain Cosmic as our two heroes, with Guise relegated the following expansion (or perhaps a mini-expansion).  

Sky-Scraper's deck will revolve around hand-size as is the case here.  She won't have a damaging power; rather, her base power will be something like Draw two cards.  She'll likely have another power in her deck which gives her a consistently damaging power.  Most of her damage will revolve around one-shots, possibly with a rider that makes her discard cards (which would keep her size in check).  A possible one-shot for her might be something like Deal one target X damage, where X equals half the number of cards in your hand.  Discard 1 card.  Another might deal damage to all non-hero targets (I picture Giganta in the final episode of Justice League Unlimited, sweeping parademons off of the Eiffel Tower), but with a higher discard cost.  I still do like the idea of her being able to do a sort of "Final Dive" against Environment targets only, picking them up and throwing them at Villain targets.

I see Captain Cosmic as something of a combination of Green Lantern and Captain/Ms. Marvel, able to manipulate and redirect energy and create energy constructs.  It'd be interesting to see him have a power (probably not a base power) that read something like Deal one target X Energy damage, where X is the amount of energy damage taken since the end of your last turn.  More likely, he'll start off with a simple damaging base power like Deal one target 2 energy damage.  With the former power, it'd be neat to have his one-shots and the like deal him a small amount of energy damage, which could stack up to be unleashed in a big blast.  I could also see him having some degree of battlefield control, perhaps with an "Energy Bubble" which would function like Fanatic's "Chastise".  It might read something like Choose one non-hero target.  That target cannot deal damage and cannot be dealt damage until the start of your next turn.  At the end of your turn, this card either deals Captain Cosmic 2 energy damage or is destroyed."

Villains:  

Again, all of this is conjecture, but let's take a look at the comics tropes (particularly the space or cosmic themed ones) that don't already exist in the SotM universe. 

I could easily see one of the villains as a take on The Brood from X-Men or Annihilus' swarm as seen in Annihilation:  lots of swarming targets, perhaps which latch onto heroes a la Gloomweaver's voodoo pins, preventing the hero from dealing damage to anything but the attached 'bug'.

We don't have anything that really represents anything like Brainiac (DC) or The Collector (Marvel), so seeing a mashup of those two would be pretty neat.  Omnitron's the closest right now, but even that doesn't quite fit the archetype.  I'd see these playing as something akin to a combination of Omnitron with La Capitan, with a fair amount of equipment/ongoing 'theft', perhaps with a condition similar to Plague Rat's "Infection" cards, representing that hero being placed in the villain's menagerie.

If Captain Cosmic is true to the genre (being an inheritor of the Green Lanterns or Nova Corps), we could potentially see his nemesis as a group, rather than a single individual:  something like the Weaponers of Qward or the Manhunters would make sense.  Plus, it seems that the >G gang is more willing to provide villains in a "deck-style" format, considering the Vengeance villains and The Ennead.  I'd be interested in seeing something like a Yellow Lantern Corps in a villainous context, working similar to The Ennead's deck, though without the reliance on the Sun/Ankh/Hand symbols.

We already have a "space tyrant" in the form of Voss (owing echoes to Darkseid, Thanos, and Mongul), but perhaps we could see something on the level of an intergalactic "peacekeeper" in the vein of Ronan the Accuser or Adam Warlock, or even an homage to someone like Granny Goodness?  I'd see his deck playing out more like Iron Legacy's or Ambuscade's, perhaps with a handful of villain targets to accompany them.

Environments:

One I'd really love to see?  Something like DC's War World or Marvel's Battleworld (from Secret Wars)--a great arena where heroes and villains show down for a cheering crowd, coupled with alien beasts thrown in to even the measure.  One neat card for this sort of environment would represent the crowd's approval:  if you deal more than 5 damage in a given round, perhaps you regain a hit point or deal +1 damage until the end of your next turn.

Alternatively, the crossfire of an interstellar battle might go well, particularly if it were between Voss's invasion forces and a fleet of defending ships.  I see this one being somewhat similar to The Block, in that you'd have two opposing forces going at one another, with the Heroes and Villains taking damage from both.  

If the second doesn't happen, exploring the ruined remains of a space station or capitol ship could be a lot of fun.  I'd worry about the similarities to the Mobile Defense Platform, but I still think there's room for some great differences, especially if the creatures that took down the ship/station were still lurking aboard!

PlatinumWarlock wrote:
I see Captain Cosmic as something of a combination of Green Lantern and Captain/Ms. Marvel, able to manipulate and redirect energy and create energy constructs.  
I think he's going to resemble GL in narrative role but not in powers; a more direct analogue would be Marvel's Nova.  As others have pointed out to me, if you combine Unity with the Argent Adept you basically have Green Lantern's powerset; it's fairly unlikely that they'll do any other heroes that manufacture targets the way Unity does, or build a "machine" of cards activating other cards that activate other cards like the Adept.  The latter is vague enough that I probably can't rule it out entirely, but still.

I disagree.  Nova's power set really revolves mostly around interstellar flight and some minor superpowers already well-emphasized by Legacy's archetype.  Nova's power set contains the following, according to Wikipedia:

The Nova Force can grant the recipient (to varying degrees depending upon rank) various abilities including superhuman strength, speed, reflexes, and perception. It also grants flight at faster than light speed, a healing factor, and energy powers. These energy powers include the ability to create an electromagnetic beam or a gravimetric pulse. It can also be used to create Star Gates. The link to the Worldmind allows the wearer to access enemy profiles, analyze an attacker's strengths and weaknesses, interface with computers, analyze energy signatures, create shields against mental attacks and receive transmissions from nearby sources.

So, in essence, a Nova Corps member's powers echo pretty much anything that Legacy (particularly Young Legacy) already does, minus the Worldmind link-up.  The most recent animated version of Nova–Sam Alexander from the Ultimate Spider-Man–emphasizes his role as "The Human Rocket" and his ability to fly at near light-speed.  Again, nothing really that a speedster-type character (i.e. Tachyon) doesn't already do.

Captain Marvel (Carol Danvers) has the energy absorption angle, which really isn't something that the Nova Corps does, and has yet to be replicated in the SotM universe.  With her recent popularity, I could easily see Captain Cosmic filling her archetype.  Combining her power-set with Green Lantern provides a neat combo that fits neatly into the cosmic genre.

Building light constructs doesn't have to be done the passive, end-of-turn way that Unity does.  I could easily see Captain Cosmic creating a "Hard Light Cannon" that can then be used as a high-damage power, with the drawback of having hit points and being treated as a hero target, so that it could be destroyed both by Ongoing destruction and by taking damage.  Plus, you could end up with a card that reads something like Destroy all of your Hard Light Constructs.  Deal each non-hero target X damage, where X is twice the number of constructs you destroyed.

Also, what's so complicated in taking a small amount of damage on your turn, to use a power based on that damage?  Absolute Zero and Fanatic both already do this, as does The Scholar (with healing, rather than damage taken).  It's certainly no more complex than Setback's unlucky pool.
